name: Document-Level Aggregation with Best-Chunk Pooling in RAG
description: Long PDF manuals are split into 50 chunks each. To avoid returning 5 chunks from the exact same PDF manual, we retrieve the best chunk per document and aggregate at the document level.
prompt:
Long PDF manuals are split into 50 chunks each. To avoid returning 5 chunks from the exact same PDF manual, we retrieve the best chunk per document and aggregate at the document level.

Execute the required analytical SQL calculation in DuckDB.
Expected output columns: doc_id, doc_title, chunk_id, chunk_text, chunk_score.
Results should be ordered as specified.
setup_sql:
CREATE TABLE document_chunks (
                chunk_id INT,
                doc_id INT,
                doc_title VARCHAR,
                chunk_text VARCHAR,
                vec FLOAT[2]
            );
            INSERT INTO document_chunks VALUES
                (101, 1, 'Manual A', 'Setup guide section 1', [0.95, 0.1]::FLOAT[2]),
                (102, 1, 'Manual A', 'Setup guide section 2', [0.92, 0.15]::FLOAT[2]),
                (103, 2, 'Manual B', 'Troubleshooting section 1', [0.88, 0.2]::FLOAT[2]);
golden_sql:
-- Retrieve the single highest-scoring chunk per document using QUALIFY
            SELECT 
                doc_id,
                doc_title,
                chunk_id,
                chunk_text,
                ROUND(array_cosine_similarity(vec, [1.0, 0.0]::FLOAT[2]), 4) AS chunk_score
            FROM document_chunks
            QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                PARTITION BY doc_id 
                ORDER BY array_cosine_similarity(vec, [1.0, 0.0]::FLOAT[2]) DESC
            ) = 1
            ORDER BY chunk_score DESC;
why_it_fails: Returning raw chunk Top-K dominates the context window with duplicates from a single document.
